_README: Rider ids that are variants of one person, and the id they belong to. CONSULTED AT INGEST: without this a re-ingest recreates every absorbed id straight from the scrape files, because the files still carry the old spelling — the same way the Dorsal placeholders came back. Lives outside the DB for that reason, like stage_notes.json and route_type_overrides.json. Produced by audit_rider_duplicates.py + merge_rider_duplicates.py; every entry carries the evidence for the claim, because a merge IS a claim and a wrong one fuses two careers invisibly. The `separated` section is the MIRROR of `aliases`: pairs a human examined and ruled DIFFERENT people. Without it audit_rider_duplicates.py re-proposes them on every run and the next --apply quietly re-merges a decision somebody already made. SPLITS live in rider_splits.json, which is this file's mirror in the other direction: aliases fuse two ids, splits fission one. Four ids were proposed as conflations on 2026-09-12; two survived checking (rider/tom-miller, rider/mark-smith) and are split there, and two did NOT (rider/paul-ellis, rider/mike-johnson) — the reasons are recorded in that file's `rejected` section so nobody re-derives them. rider/paul-c-ellis and rider/mike-t-johnson therefore stay unmerged on the evidence, not on a conflation claim.

rider/aaron-gammell.evidence: Unbound 2010/2011/2012, one rider. Two of his three registrations spell it GAMMEL (2011, 2012) against one Gammell (2010), so the source majority picks the canonical, not string length. A separate Jed Gammell rides Chequamegon with the double L and is a different person.

rider/al-thresher.evidence: One Las Vegas rider filed as three men across three consecutive Leadvilles. The decisive evidence is the BIB CHAIN, because Leadville hands a returning rider last year's finishing position as this year's number: 2010 bib 1451 finishing 29th, 2011 bib 29 finishing 56th, 2012 bib 56 finishing 64th. Measured across the whole Leadville archive that seeding rule holds for 75% of returning top-100 finishers, and for 44 of the 46 who came back in 2011 — a rider entering for the first time is not handed bib 29. Athlinks also records a location on every row and all three read Las Vegas. Finish times 8h02, 7h44, 7h53. 'Al' is the diminutive of 'Alfred', so the full name survives; the '(l)' was never part of his name at all, it is Leadville's LEADMAN series flag.

rider/alejandro-gomez.evidence: Both ids were created for one finisher of The Traka 360 by two sources that spell him differently: PCS's result page and the timer's own ranking. They are the same man because the finish times are identical to the second: 50596s in the 2024 edition, PCS rank 83. PCS's own slug is alejandro-gomez1, and PCS appends that digit only when the bare slug already belongs to someone else. Keeping our locally-minted `alejandro-gomez` would leave a name-shaped id for a rider PCS calls something else, which a later import of that OTHER Alejandro Gomez would land on. The PCS id survives even though it holds no result.

Our two ids hold exactly the career those sources describe: the full-name id has The Traka 360 2023 (2nd, club PAS Normal Studios) and 2024 (5th, PAS Racing); the short id has Unbound 2024 3rd, which Cyclingnews reports as his breakthrough, and The Traka 360 2025, which he won solo, plus Unbound 2025 and 2026, Big Sugar 2025 and Sea Otter 2026.

rider/todd-w-mcfadden.evidence: 'Todd Mcfadden' / 'Todd W Mcfadden' differ only by a middle initial only, they never appear on the same stage, and the birth years the sources imply agree (1966, 1966). That last test is the one carrying the weight: an initial or a generational suffix is exactly what WOULD distinguish a father from a son, so every pair whose implied birth years sat further apart than age-rounding error was left unmerged rather than assumed.

rider/todd-wells-specialized.evidence: Todd Wells won Leadville in 2011 and 2016 under one id and 2014 under the other, which is the whole problem: the race's own winner list was split in two. 'Todd Wells-Specialized' is his surname with a sponsor glued to it by the Athlinks registration, not a different name -- a sponsor suffix cannot distinguish two people the way a middle initial can, which is why this one is merged where the other twelve held-back pairs are not. Ages 38 in 2014 and 39 in 2015 give 1976, matching the survivor's stored birth year.

rider/yuki-saito.evidence: One man, and LEADVILLE ITSELF says so. Leadville seeds a returning rider with last year's finishing position as this year's bib — a rule that holds for 75% of returning top-100 finishers — and the chain here is unbroken across five consecutive links: 21st in 2008 -> bib 21 in 2009 -> 18th -> bib 18 in 2010 -> 11th -> BIB 11 IN 2011, which is the year the surname changes. The race handed 'Yuki Ikeda' a number earned by 'Yuki Saito' the previous August. The chain then continues 27th -> bib 27 in 2012 -> 17th -> bib 17 in 2013. Athlinks' racerId 303722365 sits on all nine rows independently, every row carries the same unusual locality 'Omeshi' (Ome-shi, Tokyo), and the finish times run continuously across the change (26,440s in 2010, 26,246s in 2011). Implied birth years cluster 1979-1982, inside the documented age noise. This is a SURNAME CHANGE, not a nickname, and the reason for it is the rider's own business and is not recorded here. yuki-ikeda is canonical because it is his current name, carried from 2011 to 2022. Checked for a collision: there is no professional 'Yuki Ikeda' on PCS (the nearest, Mizuki Ikeda, is a different name and slug), so this locally-minted id will not be landed on by a future road import — the alejandro-gomez1 hazard does not apply.

hugo-simon|simon-hugot.evidence: NOT the same person, despite an identical Traka 2024 finish time of 54014s. PCS's page reads 'Simon Hugo' with the team UVCA Troyes, and Hugo Simon is a real French rider with his own PCS page at that team. The official timer's 737-man field contains no Hugo Simon at all -- it has SIMON HUGOT (FR, club La Nuit Noire) at exactly that time, and Hugot has no PCS page. The likeliest reading is that PCS matched the finisher's name to the wrong rider in its own database, and the team it shows is that other rider's. Merging would fuse a French road rider's identity into a gravel finisher who is not him.

jeff-a-bradley|jeff-bradley.evidence: Two different Jeff Bradleys, and a name sweep will keep proposing them because one is 'Jeff A Bradley' and the other 'Jeff Bradley'. rider/jeff-bradley IS the 7-Eleven professional -- born 29 May 1961 in Davenport, Iowa, Giro d'Italia 1985, Tour de France 1987 -- and he really did ride Chequamegon afterwards, which is the part that looks wrong and is not. Athlinks records a location per row: his 2012 entry reads Davenport, IA, and 2013, 2014, 2016, 2017 and 2018 all read Davenport. Eight of his nine recorded Chequamegon ages match a 29 May 1961 birthday exactly (47, 49, 50, 52, 53, 55, 56, 57; only 2012's 50 is a year out), and his bibs are 12 to 17 in most years, which is elite seeding at a race with thousands of entrants. rider/jeff-a-bradley is somebody else: Chequamegon 2002 and 2003 only, bibs 197 and 376, location Wisconsin, no age recorded. Different state, different decade, mid-pack bibs.

jeff-hall|jeff-hall-herbalife.evidence: Two different Jeff Halls, and the birth-year fix is what made that positive rather than unknown. rider/jeff-hall now implies 1976 in TWELVE of its fifteen aged rows; rider/jeff-hall-herbalife implies 1967 in its one. Nine years apart with that much agreement behind the first number is not age noise. The Herbalife suffix is a sponsor, so the names are identical -- which is exactly why this needs recording: nothing in a name sweep will ever tell them apart.

jonathan-homberg|jonathan-van-den-berg.evidence: NOT the same person, despite an identical Traka 2024 finish time of 51336s. Jonathan van den Berg is a real Dutch road professional, active 2022-2025, with his own PCS rider page; PCS's Traka 2024 page lists him. The timer's full 737-man field has no van den Berg anywhere -- at that exact time it has JONATHAN HOMBERG (DE), who has no PCS page. Same first name, different surname, different nationality. Same-second finishes are ordinary in a mass-start gravel race, so the shared time is not evidence of identity here; the pattern matches PCS mis-linking a finisher to an existing rider page.

paul-c-ellis|paul-ellis.evidence: At least two Paul Ellises exist and rider/paul-ellis has already absorbed one of them. A merge on 2026-09-11 folded rider/paul-L-ellis into it; this is rider/paul-C-ellis. Two different middle initials cannot be one man, so whichever way that first merge went, adding this one would definitely fuse two people. The ages cannot arbitrate -- 1983 against 1980 is inside the noise floor -- and that is the point: the initials are the only discriminating information in the record, and they discriminate.
